links.note: Was 30630 (alpine climate of the Himalayas), which has nothing to do with the item: it asks for the word 'resilience', the capacity to withstand or recover from climate disasters. This chapter's 21 concepts stop at fossil fuels and cover no resilience, adaptation or disaster-management material, so nothing in the closed set is right. Cleared rather than moved to an adjacent concept.

Was 30630 (alpine climate). The item matches types of climate disaster (cyclone, landslide, drought) to their characteristics; no concept in this chapter's set covers extreme-weather events or disasters. Cleared.
Was 30630 (alpine climate). The item is a landslide-identification scenario in a hilly monsoon region; the set has no landslide or disaster concept. Cleared.
Was 30630 (alpine climate). The item evaluates the NDRF's role in disaster response, which no concept in this chapter's set touches. Cleared.

Was 30633 (low latitudes are warmer than high ones), which the item never touches: it is a cyclone red-alert case study about dangers, evacuation and the NDRF. No disaster or warning concept exists in this set. Cleared.

Was 30625 (weather changes hour to hour). The item only asks what IMD stands for; the forecasting and meteorology concepts live in chapter 25956 (Understanding the Weather), not in this chapter's closed set, and 30625 is a definition the item does not test. Cleared.

Was 30645 (what fossil fuels are). The assertion is 'human activities since the 19th century have been the main driver of recent climate change', which is 30644 almost word for word; the Reason (fossil fuels and deforestation) is 30644's list. 30645 is only the origin of the fuels.

Was 30630 (alpine climate), plainly unrelated. 'Sustainable lifestyles' as mitigation addresses the wasteful consumption 30644 names among the post-1800s human drivers. The set has no mitigation concept, and 30644 is the concept whose content the item actually turns on.
Was 30630 (alpine climate). The answer - cutting greenhouse-gas emissions, planting trees, renewables - is the reduction of the drivers listed in 30644. No mitigation concept exists in this set.
Was 30630 (alpine climate). The clash between mitigation and growth is a clash over 30644's drivers (fossil fuels, industrial practice, consumption).

Was 30628 (seasons belong to both weather and climate), which the item never touches. Part (i) asks why burning coal releases CO2, which is exactly 30645's point that knowing the fuels' origin explains why burning them releases stored carbon.

Was 30630 (alpine climate). The item asks how climate change increases the frequency and intensity of floods and heat waves, and 30642 defines climate change as shifts in temperature, precipitation AND weather events - change to the pattern itself.

Was 30630 (alpine climate). The item is about glacier melt accelerated by climate change threatening water supply - an effect of the long-term shift in 30642, not a description of the Himalayan climate type.
Was 30630 (alpine climate). The item asks how knowing a region's climate pattern helps it prepare, which rests on 30626 (climate as the long-period pattern that differs region to region).

Was 30628 (seasons belong to both weather and climate). Assertion and Reason are both about climate patterns predicting where and how often disasters occur, which is 30626's long-term regional pattern, not the seasons point.
